title: Cohomology of a separably closed field vanishes in positive degrees
statement:
Let $L$ be a
separably closed field and
$X=\Spec(L)$. Then every object of the small etale site of $X$ is a
disjoint union of copies of $X$, and for every abelian sheaf $F$ on
$X_{\Et}$,

$$
H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

Consequently, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the higher
direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] vanish:
$R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>0$.
(*Source:* this is the case of Stacks Project, Tag
[0EZP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZP) that is used in this
chapter, namely the case of the spectrum of a separably closed field; the
general statement of that tag, for an integral normal scheme with separably
closed function field, is not needed here.)

proof.text: For each point v of an etale L-scheme V, apply the proved Mathlib theorem Scheme.exists_fac_of_etale_of_isSepClosed to V.hom, the identity of Spec L, and v; the base equation holds since Spec L is a singleton. This gives a section l_v with image exactly {v}. FormallyUnramified.isOpenImmersion_of_comp makes each l_v an open immersion, since its composite with the etale structure map is the identity. The images cover V and are pairwise disjoint. Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of gives the claimed coproduct, indexed by the type of points V.left in universe u. The argument also covers V empty. This is a direct Mathlib implementation of the etale classification over [def-kun-separably-closed] on [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], without transporting to a residue-field fibre.

Apply [lem-sf-separably-closed-sections-preserve-epi], the already proved PointCohomology terminal lifting interface, to an epimorphism phi of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For each rational-point component g_v : Spec L -> V, choose a lift of the restriction of the given quotient section. The jointly surjective family g_v is a covering. To check compatibility, consider maps from an etale Z into two components with equal composites into V. If Z is empty, the empty-cover sheaf axiom makes its sections unique. Otherwise choose z in Z: the singleton image formulas force the two component indices to agree, and monicity of that component forces the two maps to agree. Thus the local lifts form a matching family, and Scheme.isSheafFor_ofArrows glues them. Naturality of phi and separatedness of the quotient sheaf show that the glued section maps to the desired section. This proves the private helper surjective_sections_of_epi on every object, including the empty one.

proof.text: Identify [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] with terminal evaluation using Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections and Scheme.isTerminalEtalePoint. Transfer preservation of epimorphisms from [lem-sf-separably-closed-sections-preserve-epi]. Global sections is additive and preserves kernels, the latter by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1) and its right-adjoint instance. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology give exactness. The proved source comparison Functor.singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso identifies the total derived global sections of F[0] with Γ(F)[0]. Apply degree-q homology. For q>0, DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE shows the latter homology is zero. Transport through the comparison to obtain exactly [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

Fix arbitrary f : Spec L -> Y. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and the section formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], each component of f_*phi is phi evaluated on an etale L-scheme. The private helper of step 2 makes this component surjective. Objectwise surjectivity implies local surjectivity, so [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] shows that f_*phi is an epimorphism. The direct image is additive and preserves kernels by its right-adjoint instance and [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1). The same Mathlib exactness APIs used in step 3 make it preserve finite colimits. The proved Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusIsoMapDerivedCategoryPlus followed by Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor identifies Rf_*(F[0]) with (f_*F)[0]. Apply bounded-below degree-q homology and DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE to conclude for q>0. This uses the exact-functor case of the derived-functor uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], not an additional resolution theorem. No finiteness, torsion, quasi-compactness or condition on f is introduced.

lean.statement: theorem sepClosedField_etale_decomposition_and_vanishing (L : Type u) [Field L] [IsSepClosed L] : (∀ V : (Spec (.of L)).Etale, ∃ (I : Type u) (ι : I → (Spec (.of L) ⟶ V.left)), (∀ i : I, ι i ≫ V.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of L))) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk V.left ι))) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of L)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℤ), 0 < q → IsZero ((cohomology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (Spec (.of L)) q).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))) ∧ (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ Y) (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of L)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℤ), 0 < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) q).obj ((lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))))

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $L$ be a
separably closed field and
$X=\Spec(L)$. Then every object of the small etale site of $X$ is a
disjoint union of copies of $X$, and for every abelian sheaf $F$ on
$X_{\Et}$,

$$
H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

Consequently, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the higher
direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] vanish:
$R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>0$.

proof.text:
*Step 1 (etale $L$-schemes).* An etale morphism is locally of finite
presentation, so an etale $L$-scheme is a disjoint union of affine pieces
which are etale and of finite presentation over $L$, hence etale and of
finite type. An etale finite type scheme over a field is finite over that
field, and a finite etale algebra over a field is a product of finite
separable field extensions; since $L$ is separably closed
([def-kun-separably-closed]) each of those extensions is $L$ itself.
Hence every object of the small etale site of $X$,
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site], is a disjoint
union of copies of $X$.

*Step 2 (the global sections functor is exact).* By Step 1 every object
of $X_{\Et}$ is a coproduct of copies of the terminal object $X$, and for
a coproduct the sheaf axiom gives
$F(\coprod_jX)\cong\prod_jF(X)$ for a sheaf $F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. In particular every covering of $X$
contains a summand mapping isomorphically onto $X$, so a section of a
quotient sheaf admits a lift over $X$: the global sections functor
$\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)$ is evaluation at $X$, and the exactness of the
sequence of sheaves gives exactness after evaluation. Hence
$\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)$ is exact, and its derived functors of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] vanish in positive degrees.

*Step 3 (higher direct images).* Let $U\to Y$ be etale. Then
$X\times_YU\to X$ is etale (base change of an etale morphism), so it is a
disjoint union of copies of $X$ by Step 1, and

$$
H^q\bigl((X\times_YU)_{\Et},F\bigr)
=\prod\nolimits_jH^q(X_{\Et},F)=0\qquad(q>0)
$$

by Step 2, cohomology of a disjoint union being the product of the
cohomologies. Hence the presheaf $U\mapsto H^q(X\times_YU,F)$ vanishes for
$q>0$, and therefore so does its sheafification, which is
$R^qf_*F$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].
